alert:
OT network monitor alert - Purdue Level 1/2
Source: EWS-03 (engineering workstation, 10.50.2.13)  Destination: PLC-07 (water treatment dosing, 10.50.1.27)
02:41:05 Modbus/TCP function code 16 (Write Multiple Registers) to holding registers 40001-40010 (chlorine dosing setpoints). New values exceed engineering limits by 300%.
02:41:19 Vendor protocol command: change PLC operating mode RUN -> PROGRAM
02:42:02 Program download to PLC-07 (logic block OB1 modified)
No approved change request or maintenance window. Operator HMI-02 shows no alarm because alarm thresholds on the same PLC were modified at 02:40:51.

triage.summary: An unapproved change was made from engineering workstation EWS-03 to water-treatment PLC-07: chlorine dosing setpoints were written 300% above engineering limits, the PLC was switched from RUN to PROGRAM mode, and a modified logic block (OB1) was downloaded, after alarm thresholds had been altered to suppress HMI alarms.
triage.severity_reason: Unapproved modification of water-treatment chlorine dosing setpoints and PLC logic, with alarm suppression, poses an immediate risk of process disruption and potential public-health or environmental harm.
behaviors: writing out-of-range setpoints to PLC holding registers via Modbus/TCP
changing PLC operating mode from RUN to PROGRAM
downloading a modified logic program to the PLC
modifying alarm thresholds to suppress operator alarms

techniques.name: Modify Parameter
techniques.description: Adversaries may modify parameters used to instruct industrial control system devices. These devices operate via programs that dictate how and when to perform actions based on such parameters. Such parameters can determine the extent to which an action is performed and may specify additional options. For example, a program on a control system device dictating motor processes may take a parameter defining the total number of seconds to run that motor. An adversary can potentially modify these parameters to produce an outcome outside of what was intended by the operators. By modifying system and process critical parameters, the adversary may cause Impact to equipment and/or control processes. Modified parameters may be turned into dangerous, out-of-bounds, or unexpected values from typical operations.

mitigations.name: Authorization Enforcement

Role-based Access Control (RBAC) schemes can help reduce the overhead of assigning permissions to the large number of devices within an ICS.

mitigations.name: Human User Authentication
mitigations.description: Require user authentication before allowing access to data or accepting commands to a device. While strong multi-factor authentication is preferable, it is not always feasible within ICS environments.

mitigations.name: Validate Program Inputs
mitigations.description: Devices and programs designed to interact with control system parameters should validate the format and content of all user inputs and actions to ensure the values are within intended operational ranges. These values should be evaluated and further enforced through the program logic running on the field controller.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses. Perform periodic integrity checks of the device to validate the correctness of the firmware, software, programs, and configurations.

techniques.name: Modify Alarm Settings
techniques.description: Adversaries may modify alarm settings to prevent alerts that may inform operators of their presence or to prevent responses to dangerous and unintended scenarios. Reporting messages are a standard part of data acquisition in control systems. Reporting messages are used as a way to transmit system state information and acknowledgements that specific actions have occurred. These messages provide vital information for the management of a physical process, and keep operators, engineers, and administrators aware of the state of system devices and physical processes. If an adversary is able to change the reporting settings, certain events could be prevented from being reported. This type of modification can also prevent operators or devices from performing actions to keep the system in a safe state. If critical reporting messages cannot trigger these actions then a Impact could occur.

techniques.name: Program Download: Online Edit
techniques.description: Adversaries may execute an online edit of a PLC to update parts of an existing program. It does not require stopping the PLC which allows it to continue running during transfer and reconfiguration without interruption to process control. Adversaries may leverage this approach to minimize downtime and evade detection. The ability to perform an online edit to the PLC typically relies on access to a workstation with the vendor-specific PLC programming software installed.

playbook.title: Response Playbook for Unapproved PLC Parameter and Logic Modification (EWS-03 → PLC-07)
playbook.executive_summary: An engineering workstation (EWS-03) wrote chlorine dosing setpoints 300% above limits, suppressed alarms, and downloaded a modified logic block to PLC-07 without authorization. Immediate containment, evidence preservation, and rollback are required to prevent over‑chlorination and environmental harm.

detection_and_analysis.action: Collect volatile memory and network captures from EWS-03 and PLC-07
detection_and_analysis.detail: Use forensic tools to image RAM and capture active Modbus/TCP sessions to preserve the malicious write commands and program download artifacts.

detection_and_analysis.action: Query NSM:Content and engineeringworkstation:ApplicationLog for Modbus write events and online‑edit commands
detection_and_analysis.detail: Search for function code 16 writes to registers 40001‑40010 and any DET0915‑identified online edit sequences originating from 10.50.2.13.

detection_and_analysis.action: Verify integrity of PLC‑07 program and alarm configuration
detection_and_analysis.detail: Export the current PLC program and alarm threshold settings via vendor tools and compare against last known good baseline stored in version control.

containment.action: Isolate EWS-03 from the OT network
containment.detail: Place the workstation in a quarantine VLAN and disable its Modbus/TCP outbound rules using D3-NTF Network Traffic Filtering.

containment.action: Switch PLC‑07 to STOP mode and lock programming access
containment.detail: Use the vendor HMI to place the PLC in STOP, then enable write‑lock on program and parameter sections to prevent further changes.

eradication.action: Revert PLC‑07 to the last approved program version
eradication.detail: Upload the validated backup of logic block OB1 and restore original alarm thresholds, then verify checksum matches baseline.

eradication.action: Remove unauthorized user accounts or credentials on EWS-03
eradication.detail: Audit local accounts, disable any that lack MFA, and enforce M0804 Human User Authentication.

recovery.action: Return PLC‑07 to RUN mode after successful validation
recovery.detail: Perform functional tests of chlorine dosing setpoints within engineering limits and confirm HMI alarms trigger correctly.

recovery.action: Restore normal network connectivity for EWS-03 after remediation
recovery.detail: Re‑enable approved firewall rules and confirm D3-OVAR OT Variable Access Restriction is applied.

hardening.action: Enforce strict Modbus/TCP allowlists for engineering workstations
hardening.detail: Configure M0807 Network Allowlists so only authorized IPs (e.g., approved workstations) can write to PLC‑07 registers.

hardening.action: Deploy message authentication and encryption for PLC communications
hardening.detail: Implement D3-MAN Message Authentication and D3-MENCR Message Encryption on all PLC‑to‑workstation traffic.

hardening.action: Schedule periodic integrity scans of PLC programs and alarm settings
hardening.detail: Use M0947 Audit to automatically compare live configurations against signed baselines.

hunt_leads.look_for: Any Modbus/TCP function code 16 writes to registers 40001‑40010 from non‑approved sources within the past 24 h
Online edit command sequences (DET0915) targeting PLC‑07 from hosts other than the approved engineering list
SNMP SET commands altering alarm threshold OIDs on PLC‑07 or related devices
